abstract: We present a complete workflow for the determination of biomolecular structures by single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy using ptychography. To account for the prominent dose damage in biological specimens dose-fractionated data acquisition and processing are introduced. Automated preprocessing techniques estimate the probe shape and scanning geometry before the ptychographic reconstruction by utilising the shadow image inside the Ronchigram. Standard ptychographic single-particle analysis is performed using tobacco mosaic virus, apoferritin and hepatitis B virus capsids. We finally give a demonstration of dose-fractionated ptychography utilising multiple scans of the same area at low dose reaching near-atomic resolution (3.3 [A]), allowing for the automated building of atomic models.
